strengths: Well-motivated problem addressing genuine limitations of existing methods (exponential scaling, causal constraints in autoregressive models) with a principled solution via PMD-based distributional matching

Comprehensive experimental evaluation across three diverse domains (DNA, Atari macro-actions, multi-agent RL) with rigorous statistical analysis (50k bootstrap iterations), extensive ablations, and detailed implementation details enabling reproducibility
Strong empirical results: achieves SOTA on DNA generation, outperforms on 36/56 Atari tasks (mean 31.33 vs 18.01), and best performance on complex multi-agent coordination tasks (5v5, 11v11 football)

Practical contributions including clear FKL vs RKL trade-off guidance (Section 5.4), temperature tuning via KL constraints, efficient sampling techniques, and demonstration of scalability to macro-action length 16 where baselines fail
Thorough presentation with honest discussion of limitations, detailed appendices with proofs and implementation details, and clear motivation for design choices
weaknesses: Limited theoretical analysis: no convergence guarantees or sample complexity bounds; loose ELBO bound used in FKL and its implications for policy improvement not discussed; on-policy diffusion learning (Section 4.2) lacks theoretical justification

Temperature tuning brittleness: FKL explicitly prone to collapse if temperature not properly tuned (Fig. 13); different KL schedules required across domains (1.0→0.1 decay for Atari vs fixed 0.1 for Football); auto-tuning adds another hyperparameter (ε) requiring domain-specific selection, limiting practical applicability

Baseline comparison concerns: DQN-Macro and IMPALA-Macro are somewhat strawman approaches; more meaningful comparisons (MAT, MAPPO) show smaller margins; missing comparisons with other recent diffusion RL methods; 20/56 Atari tasks show worse performance than baselines

Approximations in policy objectives not fully analyzed: FKL reweighting may introduce bias with unquantified error; RKL uses single-step ratio instead of full trajectory ratio, a significant approximation with unknown impact; no ablation on these choices

Limited novelty: PMD, discrete diffusion models, and their combination are relatively incremental; main contribution is deriving FKL/RKL objectives, which is solid but not a fundamental algorithmic advance

Generalization unclear: all experiments involve discrete sequences or joint actions; applicability to other combinatorial problems (graphs, permutations, optimization) not demonstrated; limited analysis of which diffusion-specific properties (non-causality, flexibility) actually matter

Incomplete computational cost analysis: DNA memory reduction claimed but only 2.8x wall-clock speedup vs DRAKES; Atari wall-clock time comparison against baselines not provided; no clear guidance on when computational overhead is justified

Design choices lack motivation: on-policy diffusion learning (sampling from p_θ rather than q for training) benefits unclear; diffusion timestep selection (200 for DNA, 32+ for Atari) not justified; architecture ablation doesn't isolate diffusion-specific benefits from Transformer capacity
